response.query: What statistical sample sizes and pilot shipment counts are required to estimate CAC and landed cost within a predefined confidence interval for each SKU type?
response.answer: To estimate CAC and landed cost within a predefined confidence interval, sample sizes and pilot shipment counts depend on SKU variability and desired precision, typically requiring statistical methods like power analysis and pilot testing. Generally, larger sample sizes and more pilot shipments improve accuracy. Specific numbers vary by industry and product.

results.title: AI Use-Case Compass — Retail & E-Commerce
results.content: # **AI Use-Case Compass — Retail & E-Commerce: Personalization at Planet Scale**. **Artificial intelligence (AI)** is transforming the retail and e-commerce industry at an unprecedented pace, promising improved efficiency, customer experiences, and growth across virtually every sector. **Generative AI** — AI that creates new content (text, images, designs, etc.) — and **agentic AI** — autonomous decision-making systems or agents (including robots and AI assistants) — are now being applied alongside traditional AI analytics in retail. A 2024 industry survey found that 42% of retailers (and 64% of large retailers) already use some form of AI, and nearly half believe **generative AI** will be a market differentiator [1], [2]. Analysts have projected **$240-$390 billion in annual value for the retail sector** from **generative AI** alone, equivalent to a 1.2–1.9 percentage point increase in profit margins [3]. Major retailers like **Walmart** have declared they are “all-in” on AI, embedding generative and agentic tools across workflows in 2024–25 [4].
